findings.problem: The identity `quotientGaloisSubgroupEquiv K L j q • x = q • x` is the canonical simplification of the transported action. It lets the finite Galois group act as if it were the quotient `G_K ⧸ V`. It is not stated as a reusable lemma. `galoisClassModuleAction_smul` is not a simp lemma, and its right-hand side still contains `.symm t`. The two-step `rw [galoisClassModuleAction_smul, ContinuousMulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]` is repeated by hand in three places: the `hsmul` here, the `relabelQuotient` argument in `galoisClassModuleExtension`, and `galoisClassModuleAction_restrict_smul`. The last site uses a variant of the same proof. Because the lemma is missing, the final step also relies on an unguided `simpa using congrArg (@Additive.ofMul …) (hsmul …).symm` to push the identity through `Additive`.
findings.proposed_change: In FieldTheory/Galois/AbsoluteGaloisGroup/ClassModule.lean, add a lemma such as `galoisClassModuleAction_equiv_smul (q : AbsoluteGaloisGroup K ⧸ (galoisSubgroup K L j).toSubgroup) (x) : letI := galoisClassModuleAction p K L j; quotientGaloisSubgroupEquiv K L j q • x = q • x`. Prove it by `rw [galoisClassModuleAction_smul, ContinuousMulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]`, and mark it `@[simp]`. The orientation removes the equivalence, and `q • x` is the canonical form. Then `hsmul` becomes `fun q x ↦ galoisClassModuleAction_equiv_smul …` (or `by simp`). Use the same lemma in `galoisClassModuleExtension` and `galoisClassModuleAction_restrict_smul`. Optionally also add an Additive-form simp lemma, so the `simpa using congrArg …` step in the card bullet no longer relies on unguided simp.
findings.benefit: One canonical simp-normal form replaces three copies of the same rewrite chain. The `relabelQuotient` obligation and the `explicitMap2Equiv` compatibility proof can be closed by `simp`. Later users of the finite-layer extension do not have to re-derive the transport identity.
